top_stories.title: Anthropic's New Product Aims to Handle the Hard Part of Building AI Agents
top_stories.summary: Anthropic has launched a new product designed to simplify the complex infrastructure work involved in building AI agents, targeting developers who want to deploy agentic systems without managing the underlying orchestration. The offering reflects growing competition among AI labs to make agent deployment more accessible for enterprise customers. Wired reports the product positions Anthropic directly against other platforms vying for the agentic AI market.

top_stories.title: The next phase of enterprise AI
top_stories.summary: OpenAI has published a blog post outlining its vision for the next phase of enterprise AI adoption, detailing how its tools are being integrated into business workflows at scale. The post signals OpenAI's intent to deepen its foothold in the enterprise market as competition from rivals intensifies. It covers new capabilities and partnership frameworks aimed at organisations deploying AI across operations.

top_stories.title: Conflicting Rulings Leave Anthropic in 'Supply-Chain Risk' Limbo
top_stories.summary: Wired reports that conflicting court rulings related to AI copyright cases have left Anthropic facing what legal observers describe as a 'supply-chain risk' — uncertainty over whether training data use constitutes fair use. The divergent judicial decisions create significant legal ambiguity for the AI industry at large. The situation underscores the unresolved tension between AI development and intellectual property law.

top_stories.title: Mustafa Suleyman: AI development won't hit a wall anytime soon — here's why
top_stories.summary: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleiman tells MIT Technology Review that he does not believe AI progress will plateau in the near future, pushing back against growing scepticism about the pace of advancement. He argues that multiple vectors of improvement — beyond scaling alone — remain open and underexplored. The interview offers a high-level view of where one of the industry's most prominent figures sees AI heading.

top_stories.title: Opinion | Big Tech Owes Scholars. It's Time to Pay Up. - The Chronicle of Higher Education
top_stories.summary: A Chronicle of Higher Education opinion piece argues that technology companies have profited enormously from academic research and scholarly data used to train AI systems, without adequate compensation to the academic community. The piece calls for structural mechanisms to ensure scholars and institutions receive a share of value derived from their work. It adds to growing debate around AI training data, copyright, and the obligations of AI developers toward knowledge producers.

further_links.title: Gemini gets notebooks to help you organize projects
further_links.summary: Google is adding a notebooks feature to Gemini, allowing users to organise projects and information in a manner similar to NotebookLM's approach to structured AI-assisted research.

further_links.title: The vibes are off at OpenAI
further_links.summary: The Verge examines growing internal and external unease at OpenAI, reporting on cultural and strategic tensions as the company navigates its transition to a for-profit structure and intensifying competition.

further_links.title: OpenAI made economic proposals — here's what DC thinks of them
further_links.summary: The Verge reports on OpenAI's economic policy proposals to Washington and gauges how policymakers and think tanks are receiving them amid debates over AI regulation and national competitiveness.

further_links.title: Meta is reentering the AI race with a new model called Muse Spark
further_links.summary: Meta has launched Muse Spark, a new AI model signalling the company's renewed push to compete at the frontier of AI development alongside OpenAI and Google.

further_links.title: The US Army Is Building Its Own Chatbot for Combat
further_links.summary: Wired reports that the US Army is developing an internal AI chatbot called Victor, designed to assist soldiers with operational and tactical decision-making in combat scenarios.

further_links.title: Unionized ProPublica staff are on strike over AI, layoffs, and wages
further_links.summary: Journalists at ProPublica have gone on strike, citing disputes over AI use policies, layoffs, and pay — highlighting growing labour tensions around AI adoption in newsrooms.

further_links.title: App Store sees 84% surge in new apps as AI coding tools take off
further_links.summary: 9to5Mac reports that Apple's App Store has seen an 84% increase in new app submissions, attributed largely to the proliferation of AI-assisted coding tools lowering the barrier to app development.

further_links.title: Show HN: We fingerprinted 178 AI models' writing styles and similarity clusters
further_links.summary: Researchers published a study fingerprinting the writing styles of 178 AI models, revealing clusters of stylistic similarity that raise questions about model differentiation and potential undisclosed relationships between systems.

further_links.title: It's time for academics to take community action on AI - Peace Research Institute Oslo (PRIO)
further_links.summary: PRIO argues that academic institutions must take collective action to shape how AI is developed and governed, rather than leaving those decisions entirely to technology companies.

further_links.title: Gain Consumer Insight With Generative AI - MIT Sloan Management Review
further_links.summary: MIT Sloan Management Review examines how businesses are applying generative AI to extract richer consumer insights from qualitative research data, with implications for marketing and product strategy.
